verdict: Starbucks revenue fell 2% to $8.6B as global comparable sales dropped 4% on fewer customer visits — and higher store labor costs and promotions cut net earnings 15% to $772M.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales fell 3%, with 7% fewer transactions partly offset by a 4% higher average ticket; new stores kept revenue flat.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — comparable sales fell 6%, with China down 11% on a lower average ticket and fewer transactions.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — support centers and head office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment.

otherDetail: Income from equity investees of $68M and $34M of interest and other income, less $141M of interest expense.
follow100Note: Net earnings of $772M are essentially all attributable to Starbucks (noncontrolling interests took $0.1M). Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $1,099M includes $68M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income. Starbucks reports in tenths of a million; this page rounds to whole millions (reported net earnings were $772.5M, of which $772.4M attributable to Starbucks).

takeaways.title: Customers came less often
takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales fell 4% as transactions dropped 6% — a 2% higher average ticket only partly offset the lost visits. North America comparable sales fell 3% and China's fell 11%.

takeaways.title: Margins squeezed by labor and deals
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin contracted 240 basis points to 12.8%: Starbucks spent more on store partner wages and benefits and ran more promotions while selling less. Store operating expenses rose 2% to $3,724M even as revenue fell.

takeaways.title: Profit fell, stores kept opening
takeaways.text: EPS fell 14% to $0.68 and net earnings 15% to $772M. Starbucks still opened 364 net new stores in the quarter, ending with 38,951 — 52% company-operated and 48% licensed.
